#2855. Caleb Wilson out 4-6 weeks with hand fracture in big Bulls blow

The Bulls' disaster season just got much, much worse.

Caleb Wilson, perhaps the 1-9 team's only bright spot through the first three weeks of the season, underwent surgery for a fracture in his right hand and is expected to miss four to six weeks.

He injured his hand during the third quarter of Wednesday's loss to the Spurs as he tried to knock the ball out of Victor Wembanyama's hands.

Wilson, the No. 4 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, had kicked off his professional career about as well as Chicago could have hoped.

Caleb Wilson of the Chicago Bulls shoots a free throw against the Philadelphia 76ers at United Center in Chicago on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Through 10 games, Wilson is averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.8 steals in 30.8 minutes per contest, putting himself squarely in the early NBA Rookie of the Year conversation.

He was on his way to another big night Wednesday, scoring 15 points in 15 minutes before suffering the injury.

Before the season, Wilson had major expectations for his first year in the league.

"I expect to have Rookie of the Year, honestly," Wilson said in June. "I'm going to work hard. I'm going to do what it takes. I feel like this team is really good for me and how I envision to play.

Caleb Wilson of the Chicago Bulls shoots as Dylan Harper and Victor Wembanyama of the San Antonio Spurs defend, Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, in Chicago. Getty Images

It's not the first time Wilson has dealt with hand injuries in recent years.

His freshman year at North Carolina was cut short after he broke his right thumb while attempting a dunk in practice in March, just as he was nearing a return from a fractured left hand that had sidelined him for six games.

Wilson underwent season-ending surgery on his thumb, forcing him to miss the NCAA Tournament.

The Bulls will now spend the next month or two without their star rookie after a start that equals their worst in franchise history.

#2854. Anthony Weaver warns Ravens about Justin Herbert before Monday night

Justin Herbert might not be putting up the numbers many expected this season, but that hasn't changed how Anthony Weaver views the Chargers quarterback. The Baltimore defensive coordinator knows firsthand what Herbert can do and understands the problems his arm talent and athleticism can create.

Herbert and the Chargers have had their share of offensive struggles, but Weaver sees plenty of reasons for Baltimore to be concerned. The quarterback still has the arm talent and athleticism to make difficult throws and create plays when the opportunity presents itself.

Asked what he has seen from Herbert on film, Weaver acknowledged that the quarterback is still trying to find his rhythm in the offense.

"Yes, I think [Justin Herbert] is still trying to find his rhythm within this offense," Weaver said. "But you still see all the talent he possesses, particularly from a trait standpoint with just his ability to run and his arm talent."

Weaver knows that talent firsthand. He faced Herbert last season while coaching in Miami and remembers how difficult the quarterback can be to defend.

"He makes some throws where you just kind of – I unfortunately was a victim of it a year ago in Miami," Weaver said. "So, I know exactly what he's capable of."

That experience is why Baltimore can't afford to assume Herbert will continue struggling. Quarterbacks with his physical ability can change a game quickly, especially when they have enough time to let receivers get open downfield.

The Ravens have their own defensive issues to address, and this isn't a matchup where they can afford to give Herbert opportunities to get comfortable. Pressure, coverage, and tackling will all matter. Weaver also pointed to the talent around Herbert, noting that the Chargers can explode at any moment. Baltimore needs to approach the matchup with the understanding that the quarterback can make plays, regardless of what his recent statistics might suggest.

For Baltimore, making Herbert earn his production means avoiding the mistakes that give a struggling offense easy opportunities. A missed tackle, coverage bust or penalty can erase an otherwise effective possession. The Ravens need their rush and coverage working together long enough to force difficult decisions, particularly when Herbert extends a play beyond its original timing.

The Ravens have to make him earn everything. If they let Herbert find his rhythm, he can make their defensive problems much worse.

#2853. Roob's Stats: Makai Lemon shows up again and 2nd-half defense doesn't

Roob's Stats: Makai Lemon shows up again and 2nd-half defense doesn't originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

It's pretty amazing that a team that's lost seven straight games can produce any positive stats.

We've been doing this Roob's Eagles Stats column for five years now, so we've never had to deal with last-place records, long losing streaks or blowout losses. But welcome to the 2026 Eagles.

When they're good, the stats just write themselves. Now? Not so much. You really have to be creative to come up with a few.

But thankfully we have Makai Lemon, Braden Mann, Zack Baun, Dallas Goedert and a few others to start with before we move on to the reality that this is one of the worst Eagles teams ever.

MORE MAKAI LEMON: This is becoming a weekly tradition. Because Lemon has been one of this team's few bright spots. With six more catches for 61 yards, Makai Lemon increased his season totals to 37 catches for 312 yards. He already has the 8th-most catches by an Eagles rookie in a season, and he's now tied with the Browns' K.C. Concepcion for most catches this year by a rookie. Lemon's 27 receptions in the last five games are 2nd-most ever by an Eagles rookie in any five-game span and most in 86 years. In 1940, Don Looney had 28 catches in games against the Dodgers, Steelers, Lions, Steelers and Washington.

BAUN WITH THE WIND: With his second two-sack game, Zack Baun became only the fifth Eagles linebacker with multiple games with multiple sacks. Seth Joyner had four, William Thomas three and Baun and Garry Cobb had two each. In all, Baun has nine sacks as an Eagle, 6th-most all-time by an Eagles linebacker behind Joyner (37), Thomas (34), Mychal Kendricks (14), Jeremiah Trotter (12) and Cobb (12). No Eagles linebacker has had more than 4.0 sacks in a season since Willie T. had 5.0 in 1997.

OUR FIRST JOE MILTON STAT: Welcome to Roob's Eagles Stats, Joe! Milton's 24-yard run in the fourth quarter matches the longest by an Eagles quarterback in his first career start in 62 years. Late in 1964, the Eagles beat the Cowboys 24-14 at Franklin Field, and Eagles QB Jack Concannon had a 29-yard run in his first start. Jalen Hurts also had a 24-yard run in his first career start, late in 2020 against the Saints at the Linc.

GOEDERT PILING UP THE STATS: With five catches for 50 yards, Dallas Goedert increased his career totals to 440 catches for 4,984 yards. With 16 yards Sunday against the Steelers, Goedert will become the 11th Eagle with 5,000 yards and another 35 yards will move him past A.J. Brown and into the all-time Eagles top-10. Goedert also needs 13 catches to pass Pete Retzlaff and move into third place in Eagles history in receptions behind only Harold Carmichael (589) and Zach Ertz (582). With 60 catches, Goedert will be the 22nd tight end with 500 receptions. And with 16 yards he'll become the 45th tight end with 5,000 yards.

RUN DEFENSE FOR A CHANGE: Devin Singletary ran 21 times for 31 yards Sunday, and his 1.5 rushing average is 3rd-lowest ever against the Eagles on 20 or more carries. In 2016, Jeremy Hill of the Bengals was 23-for-33 (1.4 average) in a 32-14 Bengals win at Paul Brown Stadium and in 1993 Neal Anderson ran 20 times for 24 yards (1.2 average) in a 17-6 Bears win over the Eagles at the Linc. Singletary's average was lowest by a Giants running back on 20 or more carries in 75 years, since Eddie Price was 20-for-15 for 0.8 yards per carry in a 37-31 win over the New York Yanks in 1951 at the Polo Grounds.

LET'S TALK ABOUT BRADEN MANN'S PUNT (the good one): We won't talk about Braden Mann's negative-two-yard punt in the fourth quarter after he couldn't handle Rocco Underwood's snap. But despite that punt, Mann still averaged 48.0 yards per punt Sunday, thanks in great part to his historic 86-yard punt just before halftime. Mann punted from the Eagles' 8-yard-line down to the Giants' 6, and that is the 2nd-longest punt in Eagles history. The only longer punt was by Randall Cunningham, who sailed a 91-yarder over Dave Meggett's head against the Giants at the Meadowlands in 1989. Mann's 86-yarder is tied for 10th-longest in NFL history and was the longest in 25 years, since Rodney Williams of the Giants had a 90-yarder against the Broncos at altitude at Mile High Stadium from the Giants' 10-yard-line into the end zone. So that was only a 70-yard net. Mann's 86-yarder is the longest not at altitude since 1991, when Shawn McCarthy of the Patriots had a 93-yarder down to the Bills' 1-yard-line at Rich Stadium. Mann also had two punts inside the 20 and no touchbacks. Through nine games, Mann has 22 punts inside the 20 and two touchbacks. In four years with the Eagles he has 67 inside the 20 and just 18 touchbacks.

THE ROCCO UNDERWOOD STAT: Rocco Underwood's fumble recovery of a muffed punt by Giants returner Charlie Jones was the first fumble recovery by an Eagles long snapper in 22 years. On the final day of the 2004 Super Bowl season, in a meaningless game against the Bengals, Mike Bartrum recovered his own fumble after catching a pass from Jeff Blake.

LONGEST STREAK EVER: The Eagles have allowed 10 or more points in the second half of their first nine games for the first time in franchise history. Their longest previous streak of games to start a season allowing double-digit points after halftime was seven in a row in 2020. Going back to last year, the Eagles have allowed 10 or more 2nd-half points in 11 straight games, most in franchise history. They had streaks of nine straight games over the 1972 and 1973 seasons and the 1994 and 1995 seasons. The longest previous streak of double-digit second halves in the same season was seven in a row in 1967, 2012, 2015 and 2020.

FIRST TIME IN 50 YEARS: The Eagles have been outgained by over 100 yards per game during their seven-game losing streak, the first time they've been outgained by over 100 yards per game during any seven-game span in 50 years. The seven teams the Eagles have faced during the losing streak have out-gained the Eagles by 912 yards – 2,595-1,683. That's the most yards the Eagles have been outgained by in a seven-game span since 1976, when they were outgained by 976 yards from Week 5 through Week 11 by the Cards, Packers, Vikings, Giants, Cards, Browns and Raiders. The Eagles have also been outscored by eight or more points in each of their last four games, the first time that's happened since 2012 and only the third since 1976.

THE EAGLES HAVE NEVER BEEN THIS BAD IN THE SECOND HALF: After getting outscored 13-3 in the second half Sunday, the Eagles have been outscored 126-40 this year after halftime, and that 86-point 2nd-half scoring differential is the largest in franchise history through nine games. The previous largest point differential through nine games was 81 in both 1971 and 1972. Only the Ravens have been outscored by more points in the second half – an incredible 96 points. The Eagles' 86-point 2nd-half deficit is 11th-largest by any NFL team in the last 40 years. The Eagles' 4th-quarter deficit of 58 points (85-27) is also largest in franchise history, breaking the previous record of 51 set in 1935, the franchise's third year of existence. The 85 points the Eagles have allowed in the fourth quarter is also most in franchise history, breaking the previous high of 84 set in 1973. Their opponents' 126 2nd-half points is 4th-most in franchise history and most since the 1995 team allowed 129.

THERE'S MORE! The Eagles' 13 points in the third quarter so far is their fewest through nine games since 1999, when they scored just 10, and their 27 points in the fourth quarter is also fewest since 1999, when they scored 26. So naturally their 40 total 2nd-half points is fewest since 1999, when they had 36, which you could have already figured out. Since 1942, the only other year the Eagles scored as few as 40 2nd-half points through nine games was 1972, when they managed just 26.

EVERYBODY GETS A SACK: The Giants had seven sacks Sunday and the Eagles had six, and that made this only the fourth game in Eagles history where both teams had at least six sacks. In 1984, the Falcons beat the Eagles 26-10 at Fulton County Stadium, and the Falcons had eight sacks and the Eagles nine. In 1986, the Eagles beat the Raiders in overtime at L.A. Coliseum, with the Eagles recording six sacks and the Raiders 11. And in 2023, in a loss to the Saints at the Linc, the Eagles had seven sacks and the Saints had six. The seven sacks were the most by any team against the Eagles since 2020, when the Washington Football Team had eight and the most by the Giants against the Eagles since they had 12 in the Winston Justice Game at the Meadowlands in 2007. It was the most sacks the Eagles have allowed at home in 23 years, since the Patriots had eight in a 31-10 win at the Linc early in the 2003 season, and the most the Giants have had in Philly since they had nine in a game at the Vet in 1997.

COLE PAYTON, ANYBODY? Eagles quarterbacks have had a passer rating below 80 in all seven games during the losing streak. That's Jalen Hurts against the Bears, Rams and Jaguars, Tanner McKee vs. the Panthers, Cowboys and Commanders and Joe Milton against the Giants. This is the first time since 2006 Eagles QBs have gone seven straight games without a passer rating of 80. In 2006, the Eagles had nine straight sub-80 passer ratings – one by Donovan McNabb and seven by Mike McMahon. Before that it last happened in 1971.

'DOES ANYBODY REMEMBER INTERCEPTIONS?' The Eagles don't have an interception in their last four games, the 4th-longest streak in franchise history without an INT. They went eight straight games in 2012, six in a row in 1976 and five in a row in 2020. They've faced 133 passes since Quinyon Mitchell picked off Trevor Lawrence in London in the third quarter in Week 5. The Eagles have been held without an INT seven times in their first nine games. The most games in a season they've been held without an INT is 11 in 2012.

#2852. In a policy switch, the Fed says its October 2027 meeting will not see a vote on interest rates

The Federal Reserve won't vote on a potential interest-rate change at its October 2027 meeting, a departure that is part of a broader initiative from Chairman Kevin Warsh aimed at reducing the central bank's market footprint.

According to an announcement Thursday, the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee will set aside its Oct. 26-27 session for "the discussion of broad monetary policy strategy issues."

Warsh announced the move at his news conference after the FOMC met in October, though he did not specify which meeting would be affected.

In 2027, there will be seven voting meetings, with the October session set up as extra time for policy deliberation without a formal vote or post-meeting statement. The new calendar shows that the final meeting of the year will now take place in November. It had previously been set for December.

"Now, what's the reasoning behind this change? To me, it's quite straightforward," the chairman said in explaining his rationale. "Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular, and information-rich intervals."

"But it's equally important we reserve time and space, as an intellectually diverse group, for strategic deliberations—for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons, focusing, as I say, on the left side of the decimal point," he said.

Warsh has been critical of the Fed's prior communications strategy, saying policymakers spent too much time providing guidance on policy moves that handcuffed them when it came time to make decisions.

Under typical practice, the Fed meets eight times a year, following with a vote on interest rates and then a news conference from the chair.

Since Warsh took over, the post-meeting statement has been shortened dramatically. Moreover, the press question-and-answer sessions have been cut to around half an hour from their customary 45 minutes or so.

Warsh said in October that the meeting schedule is another step in his plan to streamline communication. He indicated last month that the number of nonvoting meetings would increase to two in 2028.

"I believe the setting of the meeting schedule and agenda is more than some administrative detail," he said. "It's an institutional choice, affecting the nature and the quality of our deliberations and, ultimately, the wisdom of our decisions. It's yet another change to get the conduct of monetary policy on the right track."

The FOMC next meets Dec. 8-9. Its first meeting in 2027 will happen Jan. 26-27.

Correction: The Fed's October 2027 meeting will not see a vote on interest rates. The headline in an earlier version misstated the year.

#2851. 3 thoughts as the Mavericks get their doors blown off, 133-94, at the Minnesota Timberwolves

The Dallas Mavericks (7-5) embarked on a three-game road trip with the first stop in Minnesota to take on the Wolves Thursday night. Entering on a three-game winning streak, the Mavericks couldn't get to four-straight as they lost 133-94.

The game got off to a shaky start, with Daniel Gafford committing a foul seven seconds in and Cooper Flagg tweaking his ankle less than 30 seconds later when he came down on Rudy Gobert's foot after attempting a shot. The Mavs settled in behind Caleb Martin getting some early reps at point guard and doing a fine job keeping the offense flowing. Gafford's second foul resulted in Morez Johnson, Jr. checking in, looking no worse for wear after missing a game due to injury. It was a tight game throughout, but with two minutes remaining in the frame, Minnesota peeled off a 12-0 scoring run, good for an eight-point lead (34-26).

The Mavs locked in to begin the second quarter and had a 7-0 run to draw closer. Naji Marshall, Zaccharie Risacher and Santi Aldama were a big part of Dallas pulling to within a point, but the Wolves responded quickly and got out to their largest lead of the game (14) with just over two minutes remaining in the half. Kyrie Irving nailed a cold-blooded three that made you think a run was coming, but the Wolves had other ideas. Dallas was down 67-52 at halftime.

Dallas has been good at making halftime adjustments this season. They clearly had a plan to attack the rim, with Flagg getting to the line on the first possession. Free throws were a welcome sight after neither team attempted even a single one in the second quarter. The plan was foiled almost instantly, however, with the Wolves jumping the lead to 24 points within the first three minutes of the quarter, at one point having connected on 22 of their prior 30 shots. Another blink of the eyes and this one was all but over. The Wolves looked significantly fresher than the Mavs, with everything looking very easy for the former and very difficult for the latter. The Mavs spent much of the remainder of the third quarter down by 30 or more points before limping into the fourth quarter down 103-69.

The fourth quarter afforded the starters some rest and gave some of the players who see limited time a chance to showcase themselves. Unfortunately Max Chrisite couldn't capitalize on a chance to log some minutes. He tweaked his ankle, negating even the potential silver lining of him finding a shooting rhythm.

It was a tale of two rims on a number of occasions. Dallas had a few shots go in and out, while Minnesota had the opposite luck. In the first quarter alone, the Wolves had two three-pointers nearly spin out, only to drop through the net. The Wolves had hot shooting even without the favorable rolls, connecting on 61.4% in the first half – nearly 20 percentage points higher than the Mavs across the first 24-minutes. When all was said and done, the Wolves shot 57.8% and the Mavs shot 37.2% overall.

The one part of the game Dallas had a meaningful edge on was points off turnovers. Their advantage waned a bit as the game devolved into garbage time, but for much of the game they were plus-10 or better in this category. The Mavs did show effort in this sloppy outing, not hanging their heads or giving up regardless of the story told by the scoreboard. Even with the blowout and garbage time, Dallas managed to outscore Minnesota in this particular category 29-25.

The Mavericks hung in the three-point battle relatively well in the first half, despite LaMelo Ball nailing all manner of shot from the next town over as he is wont to do. Unfortunately, the Mavs shot worse from deep as the game wore on, making the battle of the long ball very one-sided. The longball opened up the entire offense for the Wolves while the Dallas misses allowed a good rebounding opponent to get out and run.

The Wolves were rested and made the most of their reserved energy. Throughout the night they were totally in a groove getting whatever they wanted and looking like a fully cohesive unit. Meanwhile, Dallas struggled to find the right lineup and fell behind big. The game lasted 48 minutes, but it was over long before then. With two more games on the road trip, the starters at least got some rest before the next one Saturday night in Cleveland.

I invite you to follow me @_80MPH on X, and check back often at Mavs Moneyball for all the latest on the Dallas Mavericks.

#2849. How the Jensen Huang affair changes the outlook for U.S.-China relations

BEIJING — Prolonged U.S. Congressional scrutiny of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy raises the stakes for already tense relations between the world's two largest economies.

Nvidia's Huang resigned Thursday, and agreed to testify before Congress sometime before Thanksgiving on Nov. 26. House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast, R-Fla., told reporters there could be "public hearings for other people or other things down road."

"I worry this incident will deteriorate the atmosphere dramatically in Washington against China, and also export control matters, and also the Trump administration in its way of dealing with China," said a Beijing-based foreign policy researcher, who requested anonymity as academics risk discipline or even removal for speaking to the media.

The researcher warned of a possible return to a situation like that in the 1990s, when a "Chinese-American" nuclear physicist was suspected of sharing nuclear secrets with the Chinese government, resulting in a federal prosecution. The court ultimately dismissed all but one of 59 counts.

Now the bilateral relationship, supported by a fragile trade truce, faces another espionage allegation. And this time it's around the tech executive at the heart of the U.S.-China competition over artificial intelligence.

"This isn't really about Jensen," said Mitch Presnick, non-resident honorary fellow on the Chinese economy, Center for China Analysis at the Asia Society.

He noted how some in Washington prefer measures to exclude China and disagreed with the semiconductor executive's message that American technology needed to be used in China in order to remain relevant to global tech development.

Washington started to restrict Nvidia's ability to sell advanced chips to China in 2022. But the Trump administration eased many Biden-era restrictions in 2025.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's Huang advocated his views across a spectrum of markets from the U.S. to China to Taiwan to Germany.

At the peak of his influence, he shared a banquet table in September with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a summit in Washington, D.C. The two presidents are next expected to meet alongside the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting from Nov. 18 to 19 in Shenzhen, China.

The political landscape has swiftly changed, with Democrats sweeping U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3 and turmoil over subsequent reports about Huang's alleged Beijing spy connection. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair over the weekend.

It remains unclear whether any sensitive information was shared.

China's Foreign Ministry has called the "Chinese spy" allegation unfounded "smears against China."

"The U.S. should stop fabricating the "Chinese spy" narratives as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions," spokeswoman Mao Ning said Thursday, according to an official English translation.

But the immediate outcome, analysts predict, is more of the U.S. restrictions that China doesn't want.

"The Nvidia scandal has destroyed the credibility of the biggest corporate lobbyist against U.S. export controls on China," said Arthur Kroeber, partner, Gavekal Dragonomics. "There is now a good chance that Congress will tighten up those rules before the end of this year."

Looking ahead, Kroeber warned Beijing could cut off supplies of rare earths or chipmaking materials if the U.S. tried to restrict China further with the MATCH Act or Affiliates Rule. The measures could, respectively, limit Beijing's access to key tech suppliers in the Netherlands and Japan, and drastically expand export controls to include many subsidiaries.

"So when Trump and Xi meet next week in Shenzhen they will probably agree to keep the uneasy U.S.-China truce going," Kroeber said. "It will just keep getting more and more uneasy."

Pressuring China has been a rare area of bipartisan agreement in Washington. Beijing has meanwhile ramped up homegrown alternatives to U.S. tech since Washington restricted Nvidia's ability to sell advanced chips to China in 2022. And even Trump's approval of some Nvidia sales had yet to translate into meaningful orders from China.

"We are going to see the two countries start to decouple again in terms of technology," George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice, The Asia Group, said Thursday, noting "China will double-down on self-reliance."

"I begin to feel the Jensen Huang case feels like more like another 'spy balloon' case," he said.

In early 2023, during the Biden administration, the U.S. shot down what it described as a Chinese surveillance balloon. Beijing called it a weather balloon that had blown off course. But the incident delayed then-U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken's trip to China by more than four months, following limited engagement amid Covid-19 travel restrictions.

Fast-forward to the Huang affair, and "the timing is no accident here," Presnick said. "We're talking about a very curious set of coincidences, and also the fact that the information came through unnamed sources, and there were other things that were strange about it."

Days after the U.S. midterms, The Financial Times and The New York Times reported, citing sources, that U.S. government intelligence believe China's Ministry of State Security recruited businesswoman Alice Huang to gather information on then-CEO of Nvidia Jensen Huang.

"Obviously somebody was looking to do this, and they wanted to ... make the discussion about espionage, and not about American competitiveness," Presnick said.

"The U.S. is thinking [in terms of] U.S. and China, but that's not what China is thinking," he said, pointing to Beijing's trade with fast-growing non-Western economies in Africa and Southeast Asia.

—CNBC's Samantha Subin contributed to this report.

#2848. Why was Jordan Davis listening to Sinatra on his way out of Philly?

Why was Jordan Davis listening to Sinatra on his way out of Philly? originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The trade came as a shock to Jordan Davis, so on the way to the airport he did the only thing that made sense.

"On the way to the airport in Philly, I had a moment," Davis said. "You know, I try not to cry. But I prayed and I played a song, Frank Sinatra, My Way.And I think that just encompasses (my) time there and just stepping away and looking toward a new future.

"And obviously the time that I spent in Philly, I have grown so much from that. And I became a better player because of it, became a better man because of it. And it's not to say that I would ever sit there and turn my back on Philly. I don't have any hate. I don't have any bad blood against it. It's just the business of it all. It's just the nature of the beast. And I'm grateful for the time. But right now, I have another mission. I have a new city to embrace.

"Excited to give back to the community and get into the community and see what all Jacksonville has to offer. So I guess I'll save that for retirement. When I really do the big big cry."

Davis spoke to Jacksonville media on Wednesday and clips from that interview were posted on social media by Action Sports Jacksonville, which is Jacksonville's CBS47 and Fox30.

The Eagles traded Davis, their 2022 1st-round pick, to the Jaguars Monday for a 1st-round pick in 2027 and a 2nd-round pick in 2029.

"Excited to work," Davis said. "We have a good front, so excited to be a piece of it. I'm just optimistic about the future. I'm optimistic about me playing a role and being who I am and being a piece to add to this already good team. And however far that we go, I hope to be a part of it."

Davis was a four-year starter with the Eagles, a starter on two Super Bowl teams, a champion in 2024 and a key figure on the NFL's No.1 defense. He had a Pro Bowl-caliber season in 2025 but his play dropped off in the nine games he played for the Eagles this year before the trade.

Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said in a Zoom call with Jaguars media he believes defensive tackles in general can continue to improve well into their career and thinks Davis still has plenty of up-side."That was a major piece to the puzzle," he said. "It's a position that ages well, and certainly look forward to seeing him integrate here in the early going, while at the same time knowing that it's going to be a longer-term decision that we made with him.

"And so making sure that his development over these next few years is something we really think through and plan out. But I think that's certainly a big piece to the why behind it."

With the trade, Davis went from last place to first place, from two wins to six wins. And he went from the NFL's No. 19 scoring defense to No. 2.

And if the Jags' defense seems a little familiar it's because defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile was Vic Fangio's linebackers coach with the Dolphins in 2023 and runs a lot of similar stuff.

"I'm here to do whatever the coaches need me to do," Davis said. "Still figuring out a plan, still learning the playbook. … It's easy to learn. It's different languages. The structure is the same as coming from Philly. The defensive structure is the same. It's the same tree. But it's just learning the language, learning the little nuances of the play.

"It's a lot more fronts that they play here than they did in Philly with a little bit of effort (on the) grindstone, and I'll be here a little bit later (Wednesday) night, I'll pick it up soon."

Jaguars coach Liam Coen recalled coaching against Davis in college and just being struck by his size.

"Jordan Davis, competed against and coached against him when he was at Georgia in 2021 when I was at Kentucky," he said. "And I just remember him walking the field pregame and I'm wondering how we're gonna gain a yard with that defense they had there.

"A young ascending player that has a lot of freakish traits. I mean, he's a large human being that can move, that does have some rush and some three-down value."

Davis joins a terrific defensive line that also includes Georgia teammate Travon Walker, the first pick in the 2022 draft that also produced Davis at No. 13 overall.

"It's gonna be great having my brother back with me," Walker said in another Action Sports video. "If you look back at the season he had last year and the season that he's going to put together this year, obviously, he's still potentially is going to grow every day and that's something that we always preach on there, at Georgia and I'm pretty sure his coaches (with the Eagles) preached on that really as well and now, he's here. So now coach is pretty saying the same thing every day. He wants to get better every day."

The Jaguars on Monday also acquired safety Jessie Bates from the Falcons and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the Saints as they reshaped their defense for the stretch run.

"I'm a big guy too, but Jordan, he's huge," Godchaux said. "I'm excited to play with him, feed off him, him feed off me. It's gonna be special. We've got a great group of guys who were already here before we got here. So we're all gonna come together. But, I mean, we have a great group on paper. We still gotta go out and prove it each and every week."

Davis leaves a team that's lost seven straight games and joins a team that on Sunday will be going for its sixth win in seven games. The Jags face the Titans in Nashville Sunday afternoon. The Jags already had their bye so Davis could play 18 games this year.

"I think anybody who plays in big games has a certain level of experience that they could bring to another level," Davis said. "It takes a lot to go to the Super Bowl and it takes a lot to win a Super Bowl, but. right now we're in the process of just one game at a time.

"I know everybody likes to look to the end goal, but you can't see at the end if you don't see where your feet are right now. So I'm just enjoying it, enjoying the moment, looking for my first dub as a Jag, hopefully this weekend. We'll figure out where it goes at the end."

#2847. Cisco beats on earnings, says AI infrastructure revenue will double this fiscal year

Cisco shares rose in extended trading on Thursday after the maker of networking gear reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter results.

Here's how the company did compared to LSEG consensus estimates:

Revenue increased 24% from $14.88 billion a year earlier, Cisco said in a statement. Net income rose to $4.6 billion, or $1.14 per share, from $2.9 billion, or 72 center per share, a year ago.

Cisco is trying to gain a foothold in the artificial intelligence buildout after missing out on the early years of the generative AI boom. The company's stock price is up about 35% this year as of Thursday's close, trouncing the Nasdaq, which has gained 9% over that stretch.

Cisco raised its expectation for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9 billion this fiscal year, more than double the figure in fiscal 2026.

"Organizations are turning to Cisco for our trusted, market-defining technology and our expertise to help them scale, secure and optimize their environments for the agentic AI era," CEO Chuck Robbins said in the statement.

For the fiscal second quarter, Cisco said it expects revenue of between $18 billion and $18.2 billion, topping the average analyst estimate of $17.88 billion, according to LSEG. The company is projecting adjusted earnings per share of $1.34 to $1.36, beating the $1.23 average estimate.

#2846. Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks

Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

Svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

#2845. Sixers Bell Ringer: Six double-digit scorers lead Sixers over Raptors

Bell Ringer Standings:Tyrese Maxey – 3.5Jaylen Brown – 2.5VJ Edgecombe – 2Joel Embiid – 1LeBron James – 1Anfernee Simons – 1Dean Wade – 1

The Philadelphia 76ers started slow but roared back for a 123-112 win over the Toronto Raptors on Thursday night.

LeBron James sat this one out for the Sixers for sciatica management, joining Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Dominick Barlow (back) on the injury report. Joel Embiid was able to play after spending the day questionable for plantar fasciitis management. The Raptors had some notable injuries of their own with Kawhi Leonard and Scotti Barnes both sidelined, as well as Trayce Jackson-Davis and Nate Bittle.

It was a brutally rough start for the Sixers, with Philadelphia letting Toronto — on the second leg of a back-to-back — build a 16-point lead at one point in the first frame. Thankfully, someone finally told them the game had started and they came out of the gate much tighter in the second, quickly battling back to tie things up and entering the halftime break knotted at 60 a piece. The Sixers finally took control of the game in the third, with the Raptors trailing right around the double-digit mark into the final frame.

The Raptors continued to battle just within striking distance of the Sixers, but Philadelphia was able to hold on to take the double-digit victory at home thanks to six Sixers scoring in double-digits Thursday night.

The Sixers get back in the win column and are now 10-3 to start the season. They will now get a few days off before a Sunday afternoon matinee hosting the Indiana Pacers.

Until then, let's get to the Bell Ringer. We have quite a few candidates tonight…

VJ Edgecombe: 15 points, 8 rebounds, 8 assists, 3 steals, 1 block, 0 turnovers

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

With LeBron James out, VJ Edgecombe was tasked with commanding the Sixers' offense — and the sophomore was up for the challenge. This was another great example of Edgecombe doing what he can do well and not worrying about forcing things that aren't working. Edgecombe was careful and protective with the ball but didn't hesitate to whip quick passes in and out of the paint for assists, while utilizing his own lightning-fast speed and athleticism to get out ahead for easy buckets for himself when the chances arose. He was aggressive grabbing the boards and wasn't afraid to get involved on defense, even if it meant picking up a few more fouls then he probably wants to on a normal basis.

We mentioned the increased responsibility for VJ with LeBron out, and, frankly, this was a great example of Edgecome doing a LeBron impression: doing all the little things (and some of the big things) right on both ends of the floor, making an impact absolutely everywhere. It all resulted in another all-around great performance from the young guard.

Edgecombe finished with 15 points on 7-for-12 field goal shooting with eight rebounds, eight assists, three steals and a block. Yep, that close to a triple-double. All with zero turnovers. Like I said, not a bad LeBron impersonation.

Joel Embiid: 20 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 2 blocks

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

From spending all day as questionable to play, to finally being ruled available, to knocking knees in the first period and looking like his night was done… to multiple dunks and a solid overall performance. The Joel Embiid experience!

Seriously, I thought Embiid's night was likely over after the amount of pain he seemed to be in after knocking knees setting a screen. After a quick trip to the locker room, however, the big fella returned to the game and somehow looked better than he did before the knee knock. He didn't miss an opportunity to get up for a block or a dunk, kept setting screens for his teammates and simply got a lot more aggressive and efficient offensively — whether that meant knocking down a bucket, earning a trip to the free throw line, or both. There were moments where, as has been the case many times before, it didn't seem to matter what the opposing defense tried to do with Embiid. He was simply too big, too strong, or too smart. Guess the knee was OK.

The only downside to his performance was that the jumper wasn't falling tonight, as evidenced by his 7-for-17 field goal shooting, but even those were just rimming out. That's the sort of thing you just hope is early-season rust and will only get a little better — or even a little luckier — with time.

Embiid finished with 20 points, four rebounds, three assists, a steal and two blocks.

Tyrese Maxey: 27 points (8-for-13 FG), 2 rebounds, 8 assists, 2 steals, 1 block

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

It's pretty impressive that this sort of performance is considered just a usual night at the office for Tyrese Maxey at this point, but that's how it feels. It's the same way that sometimes Jaylen Brown can put up an excellent, consistent performance throughout an entire game but almost without anyone noticing. A bucket here, a steal there, an assist when the opportunity presents… Maxey is just ol' reliable at times for the Sixers. Tonight, it didn't come in the form of a complete Maxey takeover we see sometimes, but the guard just kept chipping in on both ends of the floor throughout this one with impressive efficiency.

Maxey finished this one with 27 points on 8-for-13 field goal shooting. He also had two rebounds, eight assists (including a LeBron-esque cross-court lob to Jaylen Brown), two steals and a block.

Jaylen Brown: 18 points, 6 rebounds, 2 assists, 2 steals, 1 block

(Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images)

The start of this one was not good for Jaylen Brown. It wasn't great for a number of Sixers early, but it really wasn't good for Brown. He couldn't seem to score and struggled with sloppy turnovers in the first. It was looking like it might be another rough night for JB, who had a rough outing last game against his former team.

But, like the Sixers did overall, Brown turned it around. He kept rebounding. He kept up his solid defense. And, as more offensive opportunities presented themselves, Brown started knocking down shots and, other than having a few lay-ups blocked later on, put together a decent overall performance.

A rough start after a tough overall game the other night could have been enough to mess with the mental of any player, but Brown didn't seem to let it stymie him. He turned a bad opening into an excellent 18-point performance on 8-for-15 field goal shooting, filling the stat sheet also with six rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block.

Anfernee Simons: 17 points (6-for-9 FG, 5-for-6 3PT), 3 rebounds, 2 assists

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

When Anfernee Simons is on, boy is he on. An incredible scorer off the bench, this was one of those nights that any shot coming off of Simons' hand you knew had a good chance of going in. Simons chipped in 17 points off the bench on 6-for-9 field goal shooting and sinking 5-of-6 from long range. For a team that can go completely stagnant at times when the subs come in, having someone like Simons ready and willing to knock down the big buckets is huge for keeping momentum on the Sixers' side in games like tonight.

(Frankly, with how badly this team shoots from beyond the arc at times, shooting this well from three-point range in it of itself will always earn a Bell Ringer nomination from me at least…)

#2844. From Jell-O to Philadelphia cream cheese, Kraft Heinz is putting a new spin on old favorites

Kraft Heinz is giving some of America's most familiar grocery staples an unexpected makeover in a bid to revive long-slumping sales and win back support from Wall Street.

The packaged food giant — known for brands like Heinz, Kraft, Philadelphia Cream Cheese, Lunchables and Oscar Mayer — is reinventing its decades-old brands to appeal to changing consumer tastes, particularly growing demand for protein and convenient foods, CEO Steve Cahillane told CNBC's Jim Cramer on Thursday.

"I think the mistake that was made at Kraft Heinz before I arrived in the last several years is this notion that there's a 'forever brand,' that brands can just live on the history of their past," Cahillane said after Kraft Heinz held an investor day earlier Thursday. "That's not true. But equally, brands that existed for a long time are not necessarily destined for the dustbin of history."

"You have to innovate. You have to bring new news. You have to bring excitement with your brand," he added.

That philosophy is central to Cahillane's turnaround strategy. Since taking the helm at the start of 2026, he has directed an additional $700 million toward the business and hired 400 employees. He also paused plans to split Kraft Heinz into two companies. At Thursday's investor day, Kraft Heinz projected that it would return to top- and bottom-line growth in the second half of 2027. The company's revenue has declined on an annual basis in back-to-back years, with analysts also projecting a 1% drop in 2026, according to FactSet.

"I saw a lot that was fixable," Cahillane said. "If we spent all of this year separating the business ... we would have ended up with two suboptimal businesses."

He argued that the company's resources could be put to better use revitalizing the company's brands.

One of the clearest examples of that strategy is Kraft Mac & Cheese. The nearly century-old brand has returned to growth following the introduction of products including PowerMac, which packs 17 grams of protein and six grams of fiber, and Restaurant Edition, which brings restaurant-inspired flavors to the classic boxed format.

Perhaps an unexpected innovation is Kraft Mac & Cheese Cheesy Ramen, which debuted in Canada in July to overwhelming demand. "We sold out three months' worth of stock in a week," Cahillane said, adding that the company plans to bring the cheesy noodles to U.S. shelves next year.

Jell-O is also joining the protein craze, which has been fueled in part by fitness influencers and the rise of GLP-1 weight-loss medications. Kraft Heinz plans to introduce pudding with 10 grams of protein, giving the nostalgic dessert a nutritional boost. Cahillane said the company's research and development team worked to overcome the taste and texture challenges that often come with adding protein to familiar foods.

"Our R&D team has cracked the code," he said. "The chocolate's my favorite. Chocolate Jell-O pudding with protein, I think, is going to be a real hit."

Philadelphia cream cheese is next in line for a protein-packed makeover, following the introduction of new flavors of the regular spread in September. Cahillane said Kraft Heinz plans to introduce new products under the brand next year. "We've got a big opportunity to drive protein, to steal some share from cottage cheese, and that's going to come through the Philadelphia name," he said.

Kraft Heinz shares have struggled for years, but investors are showing signs of renewed optimism. The stock has gained 7% this quarter, outperforming the broader market, even as its roughly flat performance for the year trails the S&P 500's 11% advance.

#2843. OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms

CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State's outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive.

The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU's 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week's matchup with Washington State.

"You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times," Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. "I think it's about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he's at."

The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage.

WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season.

"We don't want to let the verticals up," Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. "We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first."

WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree.

OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays.

"People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage," Dahlen said. "They're going to try and two-hand jam. If they're going to try and two-hand jam, it's like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can't do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can't do it that way.

"That's what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can't just put a safety over the top of him because if he's in the backfield, what are you going to do there?"

Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week.

Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They're confident they can challenge any defense vertically.

"The underneath throws are going to be there," Hampton said. "We got the best OC in the country; we're going to be able to go deep if we want to."

#2842. Winners, losers as Commanders upset Giants 24-21 on Thursday Night Football

Winners, losers as Commanders upset Giants 24-21 on Thursday Night Football originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Washington Commanders are still alive.

Washington kept its playoff chances somewhat intact with a 24-21 road victory at the New York Giants on Thursday Night Football.

Jayden Daniels needed to outduel J.J. McCarthy to give his team a shot. Despite throwing two poorly timed interceptions, it was a McCarthy error that sealed the game.

Washington is 3-5-1 with some hope in the NFC East, while the Giants are still on top at 5-3-1. This could be a loss they look back on as a missed opportunity, though.

Let's break down the Week 10 opener further with winners and losers:

Besides tight end Isaiah Likely's strong game, Washington's Diggs was the best receiver on the night. Diggs hauled in six catches on 10 targets for 83 yards and a score.

He most notably delivered the catch-and-run touchdown late in the fourth to give Washington the lead. And it came with a memorable celebration. Diggs did his talking and backed it up.

It wasn't a bad game by McCarthy, but he will rue some of the missed opportunities throughout. New York should've put the game away sooner after Daniels' initial two interceptions. Instead, it came down to a McCarthy heave that resulted in Rasul Douglas sealing the deal.

McCarthy threw for 293 yards, one touchdown and one pick while completing 23 of 36 passes. The offense needs a bit more juice to stay atop the division.

Every passing week it gets clearer the Commanders have a defensive cornerstone in rookie linebacker Styles.

He was tied with Giants rising star Arvell Reese in total tackles with 13, though he had more solos with five and one tackle for loss. McCarthy had a stiff arm on him earlier in the game, but he compensated with a key third-down tackle to continue adding to his first-year tape.

New York needs Nabers to take that leap at some point. He had four straight strong 100-yard performances earlier in the season, but the last two weeks against divisional opponents have brought him down to earth.

Consistent quarterback play and serious injuries have hindered his development, but he lost a fumble in this one and could've done much better on the 50/50 ball Douglas picked off. He finished the game with five catches on seven targets for 44 yards, though one 30-plus-yard play did the heavy lifting.

The NFC East doesn't have a clear favorite. The Philadelphia Eagles won't be in the conversation without Jalen Hurts, while the Dallas Cowboys lack the defense and consistency. That leaves New York and Washington.

New York's hopes relies on McCarthy doing just enough and Washington also slipping up in its pursuit to the top. Both teams have several tough opponents coming the rest of the way, so it's difficult to predict the division winner. The Giants have the record edge, but Washington secured a key result to keep the pressure on. A loss would've all but ended the season, but the Commanders now own the tiebreaker in this matchup.

#2841. Pistons vs. Wizards final score: Cade makes history in double OT win

Cade Cunningham scored a career-high 52 points, and the Detroit Pistons needed every single one of them in a 144-140 victory in double overtime against the Washington Wizards. It was not just a career-best night for Cunningham, not just one of the top-5 scoring performances in Pistons history, it was the first game in NBA history that saw a player score 50 points, dish 11 assists, and commit zero turnovers.

Cunningham simply did it all. He scored 30 points in the fourth quarter and overtime. That includes a critical 3-pointer after the Wizards had crawled their way back into the lead in the first overtime on an Anthony Davis alley-oop dunk.

The Pistons trailed 130-127 and each team had traded misses. Cunningham calmly took the ball up the left side of the floor, took a pass from Ausar Thompson, and walked into a movement 3-pointer that hit nothing but net to tie the game. On the next possession, Cade swung the ball to Duncan Robinson for what felt like a game-sealing 3 with 9 seconds left, but a video review determined Duncan had approximately 1 milimeter of his foot on the line and changed it to a two.

The scoring barrage also included critical stretch in the fourth quarter where he scored eight points and assisted another to account for 11 of Detroit's final 12 points of the fourth quarter. Cunningham also locked up Trae Young on defense with Detroit up 119-118 in the final 30 seconds of the fourth. He forced Young into the sideline, cut off any passing lane, deflected the ball, and forced shot clock violation.

Sadly, after Cade hit two free throws to make it a 3-point game, Young redeemed himself by hitting an off-balance three from 29 feet away to give us our two overtimes of fun.

Cunningham's performance slightly overshadowed another notable feat — Ausar Thompson tallied his first career triple-double. He was aggressive on offense driving to the rim, and delivered crisp passes in narrow lanes to keep Detroit's offense moving.

On a night where Cade scores 52 and Ausar gets a triple-double, how the heck was it so close to begin with? How does a game like that feature 20 lead changes and 13 ties? It was a weird game.

Alex Sarr was 12-of-14 from the floor and hit his first four threes of the night. He scored 30 points and was one of three Wizards to hit the 30-point threshold. Young scored a team-high 37 points, including a perfect 17-of-17 from the line. Anthony Davis scored 30 points and added 15 rebounds.

Honestly, Detroit's biggest issue was the same issue they've had all season. Their bigs were dominated and DEtroit really misses Jalen Duren. Washington outscored Detroit in the paint and were outrebounded. The biggest issue was John Collins yet again. He was a minus-18 on the night and it felt like it was even worse.

Collins started the overtime period at center in place of Paul Reed, who was a plus-25, and promptly was the primary factor in Detroit giving up a 7-0 run to the Wizards right out of the gate. It was ugly. Come back soon, Jalen Duren.

Yeah, the Pistons might be missing Duren something fierce, but they have Cade Cunningham. And that's enough.

#2840. Nvidia’s turmoil is prompting a rotation across chip stocks. Here's what we know

Nvidia's leadership crisis is creating an opening for its biggest rivals, as investors bet that Jensen Huang's departure could loosen the AI chip giant's grip on an industry it has long dominated.

From AMD to Broadcom and even partner TSMC, chipmakers are emerging as potential beneficiaries of the upheaval, with market watchers pointing to a possible redistribution of manufacturing capacity and a narrowing of Nvidia's technological lead.

"What you're seeing in markets now is a bit of a rotation into other advanced chip design companies, on the assumption that this will enable other companies effectively to catch up," said Mark Franklin, head of multi-asset solutions for Asia at Manulife Investment Management.

That shift comes as Nvidia grapples with the fallout from Huang's resignation, following revelations about his multiple affairs including with a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy.

Huang's departure could give competitors an opportunity to close the gap as Nvidia navigates leadership uncertainty, Franklin highlighted, adding that the rotation was already helping fuel positive momentum in other semiconductor stocks.

Farzin Azam, managing director of equities trading at Mizuho Americas, said the shift was evident on trading desks, with investors moving toward chipmakers less exposed to Nvidia's management turmoil.

"Names such as TSMC, names such as Broadcom, names such as Advanced Micro will come as winners of this because they don't have this overhang of a management disruption," Azam told CNBC.

Nvidia shares have plunged 11% so far this week, while rivals AMD and Broadcom have gained 30% and 24%, respectively.

TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia's most advanced processors, has also rallied 11% over the same period, as it stands to benefit, irrespective of which chip designer gains or loses. A rotation away from AI names perceived as risky also positions TSMC as a relatively safer play for those bullish on the overall theme.

The rotation away from Nvidia has also extended into less speculative corners of the semiconductor industry, including analog chipmakers such as Texas Instruments, Analog Devices and Infineon, as investors adopt a more defensive stance, he said.

Texas Instruments has climbed about 13% this week, while Analog Devices and Germany's Infineon have advanced 12% and 14%, respectively.

Beyond the immediate market reaction, Huang's exit could fundamentally reshape competition across the AI supply chain, according to Dylan Patel, chief executive at semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis.

Patel said Huang had personally cultivated relationships with manufacturers and component suppliers, helping Nvidia secure scarce production capacity ahead of rivals.

That advantage could now come under pressure as companies including Google and Amazon strive to expand AI chip production.

The two hyperscalers were already gaining ground in securing supply-chain capacity relative to Nvidia, Patel said, and could accelerate those efforts without Huang's influence over suppliers.

"If Nvidia can't muster the supply chain, then technology is the only competitive advantage. And without Jensen, can they maintain technology advantages? Given they're only a year ahead of their biggest competitors, it's not like the gap is massive," Patel said.

The challenge is particularly acute as hyperscalers increasingly develop proprietary AI chips to reduce their reliance on Nvidia, while AMD and other semiconductor companies race to capture a larger slice of the market.

Yet the upheaval doesn't necessarily signal an end to the broader AI investment boom.

Franklin noted that major technology companies are projecting higher AI spending in 2027, with further increases possible in 2028, signaling the investment cycle remains structurally intact even as investors reassess which companies stand to benefit.

The bigger question is whether growing competition and the proliferation of open-source technologies eventually commoditize AI capabilities, putting pressure on chip prices and investment returns, he said.

For Nvidia, the immediate outlook may depend less on its earnings than on whether its next leadership team can reassure investors.

Azam said the stock appeared inexpensive relative to its earnings growth prospects, but warned that ongoing investigations and management uncertainty could limit any sustained recovery.

He expects Nvidia's earnings due Nov. 17 to remain strong, with investors likely to focus more closely on management's plans for navigating the crisis.

The result could be a reshuffling of winners within the semiconductor industry, with Franklin saying that investors were becoming more comfortable staying invested while rotating and diversifying their portfolios, instead of abandoning the market altogether.

#2839. Donald Trump Jr. exits advisory role at Kalshi prediction market

Prediction market platform Kalshi ended its advisory contract with Donald Trump Jr. in response to his venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, also holding a stake in rival platform Polymarket, according to Kalshi's spokesperson.

Conversations on Trump Jr.'s exit began in August after 1789 Capital announced a major stake in Polymarket, the spokesperson said. It was a mutual arrangement, with both Kalshi and Trump Jr. agreeing it was a conflict of interest to keep the president's son as an advisor while serving as a top investor for Polymarket, the spokesperson added.

Trump Jr.'s departure comes after Democrats secured a majority across the House and the Senate, with the party expected to crack down on the prediction market industry. While Trump Jr. has exited Kalshi, he still serves as an advisor to Polymarket. His ties to the industry could make prediction markets an easy target for lawmakers to go after, Joseph Konizeski, a former trial attorney in the CFTC, previously told CNBC.

In early October, Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said on MS NOW that Trump Jr.'s connection to the company creates an "optics issue," but added that it has never relied on that relationship to gain favor with the government.

Kalshi first named Donald Trump Jr. a strategic advisor for the company in January 2025.

Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

#2838. 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer

CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday.

The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives.

As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer.

What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol.

Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday's game and the firing of Mehringer:

Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback's delight, but doing so under Oregon's current circumstances is somewhat obtuse.

Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois.

Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome.

Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference.

He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond.

Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change.

Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it's time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff.

Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach.

Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern's offensive coordinator. No, don't expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon.

But someone like him could fit perfectly.

After Saturday's game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott.

Oregon Ducks QB Dylan Raiola (8) throws a pass to Oregon Ducks RB Dierre Hill Jr. (6) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire) (Icon Sportswire via AP Images)AP

Raiola avoided throwing anyone under the bus but acknowledged what the question implied. Passing games are built on timing. If the quarterback can't fully trust the receivers running the routes, synergy suffers and efficiency wanes.

That's less a knock on the receivers than an acknowledgment that it's easier to develop a connection with a team's more polished top receivers than with those thrust into action by circumstance.

At times, running back Dierre Hill Jr. played wide receiver alongside freshmen Hudson Lewis and Gatlin Bair. Neither had played much until injuries hit the group.

Lanning said Stewart would return. McClellan is out indefinitely.

Much has been made about the failed gadget play in the third quarter. Many have blamed Mehringer for the play-call and the negative result hurting momentum.

Oregon trailed 14-10, forced an Illinois punt and took over at the Ducks' 9-yard line. Five plays later, Oregon moved the ball to its 47.

Oregon lined up with four offensive linemen to the far left, with wide receiver Dakorien Moore behind the linemen. Three Illinois defenders lined up on that side with a fourth closer to the box.

Raiola checked to a run play and handed the ball to Moore on a jet sweep to the right, where the Ducks were outnumbered. The poorly-blocked play resulted in a one-yard loss.

After the game, Lanning was asked whether the failed play hurt the team at that moment.

"Yeah, it's a great question," he said. "It certainly wasn't successful. There's a pause in operation there, right?"

Yes, but who is at fault for the failed play? Is it Raiola for reading it wrong and not passing to Moore? Is it Mehringer for calling the play? Or is it Lanning for allowing the play to happen?

For that play to be called, it must be accepted by Lanning, practiced, reviewed on film and further stamped by Lanning to appear on the play sheet. Then, when Mehringer calls it, Lanning must let it go through. He can hear every play call through the coaches' headsets.

If Lanning didn't like the play, he could have vetoed it. He did not.

The concept is not much different from when Lanning chooses to go for two after touchdowns. If Oregon gets the favorable look it wants, it takes the shot.

That's what happened with the gadget play. But Oregon made the wrong choice and the play failed.

Regardless of the process, had Lanning not liked the play, he could have stopped it from being called.

Oregon gained 180 yards on the ground against a team that ranked 12th in the Big Ten in rushing defense, allowing 134.4 yards per game.

CHAMPAIGN, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 24: Jordon Davison #0 of the Oregon Ducks scores a touchdown against Matthew Bailey #7 of Illinois during the first half at Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Champaign, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images)Getty Images

Still, too many drives started well before getting stuffed, putting more pressure on Raiola, who couldn't consistently deliver.

As a result, Oregon converted on just four of 15 third-down attempts.

With most of the team's top receivers out, the rushing attack needed to be special, and it wasn't.

The junior entered the game 9-for-9 on field-goal attempts and went 1-for-4. But two of his three misses came from beyond 50 yards.

Hurych missed his first attempt from 52 yards out. He made a 20-yard field goal in the second quarter to put Oregon up 10-0. He missed a 53-yarder with 6:04 to go in the fourth quarter and later missed a 47-yarder with 52 seconds to go.

"He's human," Lanning said. "The reality is, those are long kicks. Some of those are really tough. The wind's a little bit different in this stadium. I think we put them in a position that wasn't the easiest to operate, and we've been really fortunate this year."

Oregon's defense kept the Ducks in the games against UCLA and Nebraska until the offense started to come alive.

Oregon lost to the Bruins 17-15 and beat Nebraska 17-14.

On Saturday, the Ducks led 10-0 late in the second quarter. At that point, nobody knew Oregon wouldn't score again. But the defense's job was to keep dominating, just in case.

Illinois Fighting Illini RB Aidan Laughery (21) runs the ball into the end zone for a touchdown during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

Illinois running back Aidan Laughery got loose for a 75-yard touchdown run, making it 10-7 with 2:15 left in the half. Illinois had rushed for just 14 yards before that run, but finished the game with 225 rushing yards.

That production took pressure off freshman starting quarterback Michael Clayton II, who threw for two second-half touchdowns.

A dominant defense doesn't let that happen against a team it has on the ropes.

The loss was more about the Ducks' offense than the defense. But the defense got sloppy—several defenders made mistakes on Laughery's long run—revealing a lack of four-quarter focus.

"In moments today, they played really well as well," Lanning said of his defense. "But ultimately, they still had 225 yards rushing, or whatever. The final total was there. We can play better than that."

Many fans frustrated with the quarterback play have called for Smith to get a shot. The sophomore former four-star recruit flashed some skills against Portland State and again last spring.

Oregon quarterback Akili Smith Jr. (#11) looks downfield for an open receiver as the Ducks hold their annual spring football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, April 25, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian

Is he ready to take on a Big Ten team? Only the coaches know for sure. They see him in practice every day.

Even if the Ducks have no shot at the playoffs, Lanning will likely play to win, not to develop. That means he has to believe Smith can win before Smith gets on the field.

However, if Moore does not return, Lanning should at least give Smith some game reps. Lanning said he had a Smith package ready for Nebraska, so we know Lanning has some plays he believes Smith can run effectively.

Truth be told, what do they have to lose? Raiola has been so inconsistent that giving Smith a series or two couldn't hurt much.

Understandably, Oregon left Illinois dejected. It will be interesting to see how the team responds. The loss probably ended the Ducks' playoff chances.

Although a 9-3 team could qualify for the playoffs given the level of national parity, Oregon winning nine games appears unlikely.

Oregon Ducks Head Coach Dan Lanning walks onto the field following a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

With many players returning this season to make a national title run and key players with NFL futures to consider, it's conceivable that many players shut down emotionally for the season.

It's doubtful that many marquee players have any interest in playing in a random bowl game. Those headed to the NFL or the transfer portal wouldn't play in a bowl game anyway.

If the team loses its zeal, the Ducks could fail to win seven games in a full season for the first time since 2016, when Oregon went 4-8.
